pk.context: 25 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

tell: A beta-3 agonist whose absolute bioavailability rises with dose, from 29% at 25 mg to 35% at 50 mg.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability is 29% to 35%, and food makes no clinically significant difference. About 71% is bound to plasma proteins; it is cleared by several metabolic pathways, with the kidneys accounting for nearly 25%.
Molecular weight 396.5. A white powder that is practically insoluble in water and soluble in methanol.
Approved under an NDA as 25 mg and 50 mg extended-release tablets, plus granules for oral suspension. Dosed once daily.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated with hypersensitivity to it or its inactive ingredients; hypertension and urinary retention are the notable reactions.
Overactive bladder in adults with urge incontinence, urgency and frequency, alone or with solifenacin; and neurogenic detrusor overactivity in children aged 3 years and older weighing 35 kg or more.
An agonist of the beta-3 adrenergic receptor that relaxes detrusor smooth muscle during storage, increasing bladder capacity, with very low activity at beta-1 and beta-2.
The generic name begins with M and has ten letters.
